intro.title: Tranche
intro.sub: For freelancers and small agencies paid in instalments: a late PayPal payment shouldn't mean unpaid work or a missed deadline.
intro.note: Recorded against the real PayPal sandbox API (PayPal's public default sandbox credentials). Sandbox money is not real.

outro.title: Thanks for watching
outro.sub: npm install && npm start — then open the board on port 4317.
outro.note: Mock PayPal by default; TRANCHE_PAYPAL=sandbox for the real PayPal sandbox (setup in the README). Payments in this video were recorded through the Invoicing API, not paid by a buyer in a browser. Bryntum Gantt and SchedulerPro trial, watermark left visible. Repository link: on the Devpost page.

steps.text: Tranche is for freelancers and small agencies paid in instalments. When a client pays late, they keep working unpaid, or they miss their own deadlines.
Tranche makes every PayPal invoice a milestone on a Bryntum Gantt, and each phase waits for the payment before it.
On the demo clock, Acme's second PayPal invoice is nine days overdue, so the phase it unlocks is blocked, in red. Below is Bryntum Scheduler Pro on the same project.
Invoice two for Acme is nine days overdue. What does that do to the plan? Draft a reminder too.
Invoice INV-2 for Acme is 9 days overdue. What does that do to the plan? Draft a reminder too.
The agent runs on the GitHub Copilot SDK. Its tools can read the board and file requests, never change it, and our scheduler, not the model, computes every date.
The dashed ghost bars are that preview: the phases behind invoice two slide, and the banner shows how far Acme's delivery slips. Nothing has moved yet.
The agent filed two requests: the new dates, and a PayPal reminder with a friendly note. Each is bound to its preview by a payload hash, and only the owner can approve.
Apply runs inside the Bryntum engine as one transaction. The browser reports the engine's dates back, and the server checks every one.
Changed my mind? Undo reverts it through Bryntum's state tracking manager, and the card now says undone.
Now the client pays. A PayPal button payment needs a sandbox buyer in a browser, so we record a bank transfer through the Invoicing API.
The watcher's next poll of PayPal sees the invoice marked as paid. That event wakes the agent by itself.
It proposes moving the plan to the real payment date. The dashed bars show the new dates.
Meanwhile, the reminder I never sent has turned stale. It can't be approved any more, so nobody nags a client who just paid.
One click, and the build phase starts on the day the money arrived.
Every request, approval, apply, undo and PayPal event lands in the audit log.
The top bar says what is running: the real PayPal sandbox API, and a live model through the GitHub Copilot SDK. Judges can also bring their own key, or use the labelled scripted agent.
Tranche: PayPal payments that move the plan, with a human in the loop.
